source_snapshot.message:
fix(ingest): bound and confine tsconfig reads

Three holes on the config-reading path, all reachable from repo content
because tsconfig.json is repo content, and all reachable before ingestion's
own size gate — createTypeScriptModuleResolver is built at ingest.ts:1049,
51 lines ahead of the MAX_FILE_BYTES check.

1. No size cap. readObject read and parsed any tsconfig whole. A 64 MB JSONC
   file — which git packs down to a ~95 KB repo — gives
   FatalProcessOutOfMemory, signal 6, which the surrounding try/catch cannot
   catch. main skips that file as tooLarge, so this was the first pre-gate
   whole-file read and it bypassed an existing control.

2. Device nodes and FIFOs. openSync follows symlinks, so a link committed
   inside the repo pointing at /dev/zero read forever, and one pointing at a
   FIFO blocked the event loop. Both report size 0, so a size check alone
   does not help. Under MCP this is worse than a slow ingest: the in-process
   runner means withTimeout can never fire and the server wedges
   uncancellably.

3. No containment. resolveExtends only checked value.startsWith("."), which
   is not containment — nodePath.resolve clamps at the filesystem root, so
   enough .. segments name any absolute path from any depth. An ingested repo
   chose which files on the machine were read, and a config outside the
   workspace had its paths trusted.

Fixed by opening once and fstat-ing the same handle (no stat-then-read
window; the pattern ingest.ts already uses), rejecting anything that is not a
regular file or is over 1 MB, and filtering extends candidates to those
inside the workspace root.

No content ever escaped: resolveCandidate only consults an in-memory Map
built from the caller's file list, so an escaped read could not reach output.
This is availability plus unauthorized read, now closed.

3 tests, each mutation-tested. ix-cli: 944 passed, 1 skipped. typecheck,
lint, knip clean.
